Five input metabolites mapped to this pathway: arachidonic acid (CHEBI:15843), leukotriene A4 (CHEBI:15651), 15(S)-HETE (CHEBI:15558), 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2 (CHEBI:34159), and 5(S)-HETE (CHEBI:28209). Parallel m/z-direct analysis via Mummichog on the human metabolic-function network independently recovered 'Arachidonic acid metabolism' as its top hit (p = 4.2e-4) with 11 of 11 compounds in the input mapping to that KEGG-native module — a perfect overlap — and ranked 'Leukotriene metabolism' fourth (p = 0.02). The NSAID drug-action pathways in SMPDB (rofecoxib, acetylsalicylic acid, acetaminophen, etc.) all share the identical five eicosanoid input compounds, confirming that the biological perturbation centres on the COX/LOX eicosanoid-shunt. Arachidonic acid itself is the canonical substrate shared by both the cyclooxygenase (prostaglandin J2 branch) and lipoxygenase (HETE and leukotriene A4 branches) arms of this pathway. Histamine (CHEBI:18295) was independently captured by Mummichog via histidine metabolism, consistent with known cross-talk between inflammatory amine signalling and the eicosanoid network.
